entry: Temperate [[Grassland|grassland]] ecosystem in which grasses, herbs, and shrubs, rather than trees, are the dominant vegetation. Prairies belong to the temperate grasslands, savannas, and shrublands [[Biome|biome]], with similar climates and moderate rainfall. Other temperate grassland regions include the Pampas of Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay and the steppe of Romania, Ukraine, Russia, and Kazakhstan. In [[North America]], the term covers the lower and mid-latitude Interior Plains of [[Canada]], the [[United States]], and Mexico, including the [[Great Plains]]. Tallgrass prairie evolved with grazing by native [[Bison|bison]], elk, and white-tailed deer, and with fire that native people used annually for 10,000–20,000 years. Fire removes trees while prairie plants survive, since up to 75% of plant biomass lies below ground and regrows from roots reaching upwards of 20 feet. Over 90% of original tallgrass prairie has been converted to agriculture.

Genus of herbivorous burrowing [[Squirrel|ground squirrels]] native to the [[Grassland|grasslands]] of [[North America]]. Five species are recognized. Despite the name, prairie dogs are not canines; they are named for their habitat and their warning call, which sounds like a dog's bark. They are considered a keystone species. Their mounds encourage grass growth and renew topsoil, and their burrows shelter other species. Predators such as [[Coyote|coyotes]], golden eagles, and black-footed ferrets feed on them. Prairie dogs have some of the most complex [[Communication|communication]] systems of any animal. Their populations have declined through farming, urban development, and [[Disease|disease]].

Chemical element with atomic number 59, the third member of the [[Lanthanide|lanthanide]] series. Praseodymium is a soft, silvery, malleable, and ductile [[Metal|metal]] and one of the [[Rare-earth element|rare-earth metals]]. It is too reactive to be found in native form and always occurs naturally with other rare-earth metals. It makes up 9.1 parts per million of Earth's crust. In 1885 Austrian chemist Carl Auer von Welsbach separated didymium into praseodymium and [[Neodymium|neodymium]]. The name comes from Greek words meaning 'leek-green' and 'twin'. Praseodymium is used in high-performance permanent magnets alloyed with neodymium, in aircraft engine alloys, and in glass that filters yellow light, such as welders' goggles.

Metropolis (pop., 2011: 1.53 million) in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]], formerly known as Allahabad. The city lies close to Triveni Sangam, the confluence of the [[Ganges]] and [[Yamuna]] with the mythical Sarasvati, a site central to Hindu scriptures. It is the judicial capital of Uttar Pradesh and home to the Allahabad High Court. The Mughal emperor [[Akbar]] is credited with founding a city there, and in the early 17th century it was a provincial capital under Jahangir. Prayagraj hosts the [[Kumbh Mela]], one of the largest peaceful gatherings in the world. Its economy now derives mostly from real estate and financial services.

Loose association of English painters, poets, and art critics, founded in London in 1848. Its seven founding members, including William Holman Hunt, John Everett Millais, and Dante Gabriel Rossetti, sought a return to the detail, intense colors, and complex compositions of Quattrocento Italian art. They rejected the Classical poses of [[Raphael]] and the mechanistic approach of the later [[Mannerism|Mannerist]] artists. They also objected to the influence of Sir Joshua Reynolds, founder of the Royal Academy of Arts. In an 1851 letter to *The Times*, critic John Ruskin defended their landscapes and commitment to truth. The group published the periodical *The Germ* and separated after almost five years. Later followers included Edward Burne-Jones and William Morris.

Informal unit of geologic time, the earliest part of Earth's history, before the [[Phanerozoic]] Eon. It spans from the formation of Earth about 4.6 billion years ago to the start of the [[Cambrian]] Period about 538.8 million years ago, when hard-shelled creatures appeared in abundance. The name refers to its preceding the Cambrian, named after Cambria, the Latinized name for [[Wales]]. The Precambrian accounts for 88% of Earth's geologic time and is divided into the [[Hadean]], [[Archean]], and [[Proterozoic]] eons. Its fossil record is poor, because many rocks have been heavily metamorphosed, eroded, or buried beneath younger strata. Zircon crystals from Western Australia have been dated to 4,404 ± 8 million years old, and a stable crust was apparently in place by 4,433 million years ago. Bacterial fossils older than 3.46 billion years have been found in Western Australia.

Judicial decision that serves as an authority in deciding later identical or similar cases. Fundamental to [[Common law]] legal systems, precedent operates under the principle of *stare decisis* ("to stand by things decided"), which promotes consistency and predictability. A precedent may be binding, which courts must follow, or persuasive, which courts may consider without being obliged to follow it. [[Civil law (legal system)|Civil law]] systems, by contrast, rely mainly on comprehensive codes and detailed [[Statute|statutes]], with little emphasis on precedent. A precedent may be applied or adopted, distinguished on materially different facts, modified by a higher court, or overruled if found erroneous in law or overtaken by legislation. The *ratio decidendi* is the reasoning that forms the binding basis of a decision, distinct from non-binding *obiter dicta*.

Product of the condensation of atmospheric [[Water vapor|water vapor]] that falls from clouds under the pull of gravity. The main forms are drizzle, rain, sleet, snow, ice pellets, graupel, and hail. Fog and mist are not precipitation, because their water vapor does not condense enough to fall. Precipitation forms as smaller droplets coalesce with other droplets or ice crystals, and most of it occurs in the [[Tropics|tropics]] through [[Convection|convection]]. It is the main source of fresh water on the planet, falling as about 505,000 cubic kilometers (121,000 mi³) a year, of which 398,000 cubic kilometers fall over oceans and 107,000 over land. Global average annual precipitation is 990 millimeters (39 in), but over land it is only 715 millimeters (28.1 in). The [[Köppen climate classification]] uses average annual rainfall to distinguish climate regimes.

Biological interaction in which one organism, the predator, kills and eats another, its prey. It differs from [[Scavenger|scavenging]], which eats only organisms found already dead, though many predators, such as [[Jackal|jackals]] and [[Hyena|hyenas]], also scavenge. Pursuit predators actively chase prey, while ambush predators wait for an opportunity and often use [[Camouflage|stealth]] or aggressive mimicry. Prey have evolved defenses such as warning coloration, alarm calls, and defensive spines, sometimes creating evolutionary arms races. Predation has been a major driver of [[Evolution|evolution]] since at least the [[Cambrian]] period. A predator is distinguished from a parasitoid wasp, whose larva has just one host, which it eventually kills.

Doctrine in [[Theology|Christian theology]] holding that God has willed all events, usually with reference to the eventual fate of each soul. Explanations of predestination often address the paradox of [[Free will|free will]], since God's omniscience seems incompatible with human freedom; it can be regarded as a form of religious [[Determinism|determinism]]. Most of Second Temple Judaism emphasized free will, but texts from Qumran seem to be more deterministic. [[Augustine of Hippo|Augustine]] emphasized that salvation results from God's grace rather than human merit, which sparked debates over double predestination. [[John Calvin|Calvin]] taught double predestination, while [[Lutheranism]] affirms unconditional election to salvation but denies predestination to damnation. [[Arminianism]] links election to foreseen human faith, and Roman Catholicism teaches that God predestines in harmony with human response.

First-level administrative division of [[Japan]], numbering 47. The 43 prefectures proper (*ken*) are joined by two urban prefectures (*fu*: [[Osaka]] and [[Kyoto]]), the regional prefecture of [[Hokkaido]] (*dō*), and the metropolis of [[Tokyo]] (*to*). The Meiji government created the prefecture system in July 1871 by abolishing the feudal han domains. Each prefecture is headed by a directly elected governor, and a unicameral assembly enacts its ordinances and budgets. Prefectures rank immediately below the national government and form the country's first level of jurisdiction.

Period from the first human occupation of the region to the First Dynasty of [[Egypt]], around 3100 BC. Predynastic Egypt is traditionally dated from the final part of the [[Neolithic]], beginning about c. 6210 BC, to the end of the Naqada III period around c. 3000 BC. Because these dates were set before widespread excavation, and recent finds suggest gradual development, terms such as "Dynasty 0" are used for its final phase. Most sites are in Upper Egypt, because [[Nile]] silt buried most Delta sites. Humans have occupied the region for over a million years, though the early evidence is sparse. Waldemar Chmielewski dated some of the oldest known structures, near Wadi Halfa on the southern border, to 100,000 BC.

Art produced in preliterate cultures, from the earliest human workmanship with an artistic purpose until the spread of writing or other record-keeping. The earliest clear examples date to the Upper [[Paleolithic]] about 40,000 years ago, although evidence suggests the preference for the aesthetic emerged in the Middle Paleolithic. A drawing by Homo sapiens estimated at 73,000 years old was reported in 2018. Engraved shells made by [[Homo erectus]] date back as far as 500,000 years, though experts disagree on whether these count as art. From the Upper Paleolithic through the Mesolithic, [[Cave painting|cave paintings]] and portable art such as figurines and beads predominated. Pottery, sculpture, and megaliths appeared in the [[Neolithic]], and [[Metalworking|metalworking]] in the Bronze Age added media and artisans. By the Iron Age, civilizations with writing had arisen from Ancient Egypt to Ancient China.

Religious practice of prehistoric cultures, which left no written records of their beliefs. Prehistory accounts for the bulk of human experience, and over 99% of it occurred during the [[Paleolithic]] period. Religion emerged with certainty in the Upper Paleolithic around 50,000 years ago, possibly in a shamanic form centered on spiritual leaders who entered trance states, as suggested by cave art and Venus figurines. The [[Neolithic]] Revolution, around 12,000 BC, established agriculture and made societies more hierarchical, and religion may have become more centralized, including ancestor worship. Stone circles in the British Isles and Brittany, the most prominent of which is [[Stonehenge]], are a notable feature. Late Neolithic and Chalcolithic religion includes Proto-Indo-European mythology. Bronze Age and Iron Age religions are better understood through written records.

Indian actress and entrepreneur known for [[Hindi]]-language films. She made her acting debut in *Dil Se* (1998), earning the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut, and won the Filmfare Award for Best Actress for *Kal Ho Naa Ho* (2003). Her first international role, in the Canadian drama *Heaven on Earth* (2008), won her the Silver Hugo Award for Best Actress. She founded the production company PZNZ Media and has co-owned the cricket team Punjab Kings in the [[Indian Premier League]] since 2008. Known for outspoken public statements, she received the Godfrey Phillips National Bravery Award for refusing to retract her testimony against the Indian mafia.

Preconceived, usually unfavorable evaluation of a person or group based on perceived characteristics such as race, religion, sex, or [[Wealth|wealth]]. The word can also refer to unfounded or inflexible beliefs. Psychological research on prejudice began in the 1920s and at first attempted to prove white supremacy. In the 1930s and 1940s, concern over Nazi anti-Semitism led theorists to link prejudice to an authoritarian personality. In 1954, [[Gordon Allport]] defined prejudice as a "feeling, favorable or unfavorable, toward a person or thing, prior to, or not based on, actual experience," and linked it to categorical thinking. Allport's contact hypothesis proposed that equal-status contact under optimal conditions reduces bias, but meta-analyses have produced inconsistent results. More than 40 million Implicit Association Tests, which measure hidden attitudes, were completed in 2023 alone. A United Nations institute has highlighted prejudice as a global security threat because it fuels scapegoating and violence.

Indian writer and pioneer of [[Hindi]] and Urdu social fiction, also known as Dhanpat Rai Srivastava. Born in a village near [[Varanasi]], he began writing in Urdu under the pen name Nawab Rai before adopting Premchand and shifting to Hindi. His more than a dozen novels, around 300 short stories, and essays portray rural poverty, [[Caste|caste]] hierarchies, and the plight of women and laborers. Major works include *Godaan*, *Karmabhoomi*, and *Gaban*. His first collection of five short stories, *Soz-e-Watan*, appeared in 1907. He is regarded as one of the foremost Hindi writers of the early twentieth century.

Professional [[Association football|association football]] league and the highest level of the English football league system. Twenty clubs play 38 matches each season, from August to May, with promotion and relegation. Founded as the FA Premier League on 20 February 1992 after top-tier clubs broke away from the English Football League, it is the world's most-watched sports league. More than 1.4 billion people watched live games during the 2024–25 season. Its average attendance of 40,421 per game is the highest in association football. Its domestic [[Broadcasting|broadcasting]] rights deal is worth £6.7 billion, and Manchester United has won the title a record 13 times.

Branch of [[Protestantism|Protestant]] Christianity, named for its government by representative assemblies of elders, called presbyters. The tradition traces its roots to the Reformation of the 16th century, particularly the Republic of Geneva under [[John Calvin]] and the Scottish Reformer [[John Knox]], who established the Presbyterian Church in Scotland. Its theology emphasizes God's sovereignty, the authority of Scripture, and salvation through grace and faith in Christ, as set out in the Westminster Standards. Scots and Scots-Irish immigrants carried the denomination to the [[United States]], [[Canada]], [[Australia]], [[New Zealand]], and [[South Africa]]. Local congregations are governed by sessions of elders, with presbyteries, synods, and general assemblies above them. There are roughly 75 million Presbyterians in the world.

Medication that may be dispensed only to people with a medical prescription. Over-the-counter drugs, by contrast, can be obtained without one. The restriction reflects the potential for misuse, from drug abuse to practicing medicine without a license. Jurisdictions define the category differently. In [[Australia]], Schedule 4 covers prescription-only medicines, while in the [[United Kingdom]] three categories govern supply. In North America, the abbreviation Rx comes from the Latin *recipe*, meaning "take." Use of prescription drugs has increased since the 1960s. In the United States, overprescribing of analgesics such as [[Oxycodone]] fueled an opioid epidemic from the 1990s, with over 500,000 overdose deaths linked to prescription opioids and their illicit counterparts.

Head of state and [[Head of government|head of government]] of the [[United States]]. Article II of the Constitution vests executive power in the president, who directs the executive branch, enforces federal law, and is commander-in-chief of the [[United States Armed Forces|armed forces]]. The president conducts foreign policy and can sign or veto federal legislation. The office has grown since [[George Washington]] took office in 1789. The Twenty-second Amendment, ratified in 1951, limits a person to two elected terms. Nine vice presidents have become president through the death or resignation of a predecessor. [[Donald Trump]] is the 47th president, in office since January 20, 2025.

Force applied perpendicular to the surface of an object, per unit area over which the force is distributed. Pressure is symbolized *p* or *P*, and gauge pressure is measured relative to ambient pressure. The SI unit is the [[Pascal (unit)|pascal]] (Pa), equal to one [[Newton (unit)|newton]] per square meter. Other units include pounds per square inch (psi) and the [[Bar (unit)|bar]]. The [[Atmosphere|atmosphere]] (atm) is defined as standard atmospheric pressure, and the torr is 1/760 of it. In fluids, hydrostatic pressure increases linearly with depth, following P = ρgh, where ρ is density, g is gravitational acceleration, and h is depth. Atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately 101,325 Pa.

Legal principle that a person accused of a crime is considered innocent until proven guilty. The prosecution bears the burden of proof and must generally show guilt beyond a reasonable doubt; if doubt remains, the accused must be acquitted. The opposite system is a presumption of guilt. The principle is a legal right in criminal trials under [[Common law]] and [[Civil law (legal system)|civil law]] systems, and an international human right under Article 11 of the [[Universal Declaration of Human Rights]]. The sixth-century Digest of Justinian stated that proof lies on the one who asserts, not on the one who denies, and Talmudic and Islamic law also emphasized the innocence of the accused until proved guilty. In the early 13th century, [[Louis IX of France|Louis IX]] banned trials by ordeal and introduced the presumption into criminal procedure, though torture soon returned. [[William Blackstone]] argued that it is better that ten guilty persons escape than that one innocent suffer.

Executive capital of [[South Africa]], seat of the executive branch of government and host to all foreign embassies in the country. Pretoria hosts the headquarters of all national government departments and agencies. It is home to 134 foreign embassies and high commissions, the second-largest concentration of diplomatic missions in the world after [[Washington, D.C.]] The city was founded in 1855 by Marthinus Pretorius, a Voortrekker leader, and named after his father Andries Pretorius, a national hero of the Voortrekkers. It became the administrative capital of the Union of South Africa in 1910 and remained so when the country became a republic in 1961. Pretoria is also a center of research, home to the University of Pretoria and the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research. It is known as the Jacaranda City for its many jacaranda trees.

Application of healthcare measures to prevent the occurrence of disease, also called prophylaxis. Prevention is classified as primal, primary, secondary, or tertiary, and includes vaccines, screening tests, and counseling. Hugh R. Leavell and E. Gurney Clark coined the term primary prevention in the 1940s and later expanded the levels to include secondary and tertiary prevention. According to estimates by the [[World Health Organization|WHO]], about 55 million people died worldwide in 2011, and two-thirds of these deaths were from noncommunicable diseases. Common screenings include checks for hypertension, [[Breast cancer|breast cancer]] by mammography, a [[Pap test]] for cervical cancer, and screening for osteoporosis. Global [[Vaccine|vaccination]] campaigns are estimated to have prevented 154 million deaths over the past half-century. Overdiagnosis can lead to overtreatment, and the cost-effectiveness of preventive care remains debated.
